- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After recent price spikes, model often overshoots downward in next period; apply mild upward adjustment to prevent premature reversal.
- If sentiment shows strong positive spikes (e.g., +0.61), model frequently underreacts; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment peaks.
- Model consistently underestimates true price decline in early 30d horizon; apply 2–3% upward bias to first 5–7 days of forecast if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment is stable or mildly negative, model tends to lag true mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent history.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to reflect it; add 1–2% downward bias to later forecast days.
